overview.problemStatement: The API shell is largely built - a global ValidationPipe, a global HttpExceptionFilter, the Swagger document, the global ConfigModule and a throttler all exist on main.ts and app.module.ts - but two gaps remain and both stay invisible until something breaks. First, there is no structured logging: NestFactory.create uses Nest's default console logger, so output is unstructured text with no request correlation and no redaction, and searching the codebase for pino returns zero hits. When a request fails in production an operator cannot tell which lines belong to it, and a careless log call can print a bearer token into a sink that outlives the incident. Second, CI has never passed: the workflow runs the right five gates but omits prisma generate, so on a clean checkout @prisma/client exports nothing and pnpm typecheck fails with "no exported member PrismaClient"; both historical main runs are red.
overview.proposedSolution: Add structured JSON logging with nestjs-pino: one line per request carrying a generated request id, method, url, status and duration; the same id on every line written while handling it; an X-Request-Id response header; and redaction of authorization, cookie and password fields before anything is serialised. Call sites keep Nest's Logger interface, so application code does not learn a second logging API. Make CI honest by adding the Prisma client generation step and the two hardening steps the auth feature's security report asked for - a production dependency audit and a secret scan.
overview.targetAudience: Operators on call, who need one JSON line per request and a way to follow a single failing request end to end; every later feature, which will log through this and would otherwise invent its own scheme; reviewers, who currently take 'lint and typecheck pass locally' on trust because no CI run has ever succeeded.
assumptions: No log shipping or aggregation infrastructure exists or is in scope; logs go to stdout as JSON, which is what a container platform collects.
nestjs-pino is the appropriate choice because it is the Nest integration for pino and keeps the Logger interface at call sites. It is a new runtime dependency.

The server test suite needs neither PostgreSQL nor Redis in CI: it runs against the in-memory Prisma double and the Redis-gated suite skips itself. If that proves false, the workflow gains service containers in this feature rather than failing silently.
CI runs Node 20, as .github/workflows/ci.yml already declares.
outOfScope: Log aggregation, retention, shipping or dashboards (Loki, Datadog, ELK).
Metrics and distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry); correlation ids are not spans.
Changing the exception body shape, the validation rules or any status code.
GitHub branch-protection settings, which are a repository setting rather than code.
Rewriting call sites to a new logger API: existing Logger usage keeps working.

userStories.title: An operator can follow one request through the logs
userStories.role: engineer woken up by an alert
userStories.want: each request to be one structured record with an id I can search on
userStories.benefit: I can reconstruct a failure without reading interleaved prose

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a request to any API route, when it completes, then exactly one JSON object is written to stdout with reqId, req.method, req.url, res.statusCode and responseTime.
Given a request, when the handler logs through Nest's Logger, then those lines carry the same reqId as the request record, and the response carries a matching X-Request-Id header.
Given a request carrying an Authorization header, a Cookie header and a body with a password, when the request record and handler logs are written, then none of those values appears in the output.
Given LOG_LEVEL is set, when the server starts, then that level is honoured; with no value it defaults to info. A 5xx response logs at error, a 4xx at warn, everything else at info.

userStories.title: A broken change cannot merge
userStories.want: the pipeline to run every gate on a pull request and fail loudly
userStories.benefit: 'it passes locally' stops being the only evidence

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a clean checkout, when the CI workflow runs, then install, Prisma client generation, lint, typecheck, test and build all succeed and the run is green.

Given a clean checkout without a generated Prisma client, when pnpm typecheck runs, then it fails; the workflow must therefore generate the client before typechecking. The step is load-bearing, not ceremonial.
Given the workflow, when it runs, then a production dependency audit and a secret scan execute, and a high or critical finding fails the job.

userStories.title: The existing API contract is preserved
userStories.want: the validation and error behaviour I already depend on to keep working
userStories.benefit: the shell can change around me without breaking me

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a request body with an unknown property, when it is validated, then the API still returns 400 and rejects the request (whitelist and forbidNonWhitelisted unchanged).
Given a thrown HttpException, when the exception filter handles it, then the response body keeps its existing statusCode and message shape and now also carries requestId.
Given Swagger is enabled, when the app starts, then /api/docs still serves the document and logging does not alter that route.

functionalRequirements.text: The server MUST emit one structured JSON log record per HTTP request containing a request id, method, url, status code and duration.
The request id MUST be attached to every log line written while that request is handled, and MUST be returned in an X-Request-Id response header.
Log output MUST redact authorization, cookie, set-cookie, password, passwordHash and token values at any depth.
The log level MUST come from LOG_LEVEL defaulting to info, and response severity MUST map 5xx to error, 4xx to warn and otherwise info.
The CI workflow MUST generate the Prisma client after install and before typecheck.
The CI workflow MUST run a production dependency audit and a secret scan, failing on high or critical findings.
The global ValidationPipe MUST keep whitelist, forbidNonWhitelisted and transform enabled.
HttpExceptionFilter MUST keep its current response shape and add requestId.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Logging MUST NOT add more than 5 ms to p95 latency on a local run of the health endpoint, measured before and after the change.
Each record MUST be valid JSON on a single line in every environment, so a collector parses it without a multi-line pattern.
The CI job MUST finish in under 15 minutes on ubuntu-latest so a pull request is not blocked by the pipeline itself.
Adding logging MUST NOT require changing call sites: existing Logger calls keep compiling and working.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Fall back to info and log one warning naming the invalid value; never crash on startup.

edgeCases.description: A client sends its own X-Request-Id header.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Accept it only if it is a safe token (bounded length, A-Za-z0-9-_); otherwise generate a new id. Never echo arbitrary client input into logs or headers unvalidated.

edgeCases.description: The health endpoint is polled every second.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Still one record per request, at info; no per-request handler chatter. Volume is an operational concern, not a reason to skip the record.
Logging is silenced under NODE_ENV=test so fifty passing tests do not produce thousands of lines; the logging test opts back in.

edgeCases.description: A log call receives a circular object.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Serialise safely, and never throw from a logging call - a failed log must not fail the request.

dependencies.name: nestjs-pino
dependencies.notes: New runtime dependency: the Nest integration for pino, providing LoggerModule and the Logger service. Added together with pino-http.

dependencies.name: pino-pretty
dependencies.notes: Development-only human-readable output. Never required in CI, so a missing devDependency cannot break the pipeline.

dependencies.name: @nestjs/common Logger
dependencies.notes: Existing call sites keep this interface (NFR-004); the pino integration supplies the implementation behind it.

dependencies.name: GitHub Actions
dependencies.notes: pnpm/action-setup@v4, actions/setup-node@v4 and the secret-scan action; the workflow already exists and gains steps rather than being replaced.

risks.description: A new dependency brings a CVE into the runtime.
risks.mitigation: pnpm audit --prod runs in CI from this feature on (FR-006); the version is pinned in the lockfile.

risks.description: Redaction misses a nested field and a token reaches the log sink.
risks.mitigation: AC-003 asserts on nested paths, not only top-level headers, and the redact list is one constant reviewed in the diff.

risks.description: CI minutes balloon with the audit and scan steps.
risks.mitigation: NFR-003 caps the job at 15 minutes; the audit is --prod only and the scan is diff-scoped.

risks.description: Logging becomes a latency tax on every request.
risks.mitigation: NFR-001 measures p95 before and after; pino writes asynchronously to stdout.

risks.description: Tests get noisy and slow from per-request records.
risks.mitigation: EC-004 silences logging under NODE_ENV=test; the logging test opts back in explicitly.
